window.note: 14 calendar days (10 trading days) of development data already used by Phases 5-5.2; not sealed, not forward.

rules: INCONCLUSIVE if fewer than 15 M5 trades (or not screened for lack of an indicator).
REJECTED if M5 expectancy after costs <= 0, or the concept is unsuitable for GoldScalp's data or its own source shows it unprofitable.
WORTH FURTHER RESEARCH only if M5 expectancy > 0, PF >= 1.1, still positive without its best day, positive with costs x2, and M15 execution not negative.

why: positive (+0.013 R over 22 trades) but fails: positive without the best day, positive with costs x2
Needs the session/day open, a 10-day stretch average and NR4/NR7 day ranges; no such levels exist in the builder. The documented version is a multi-day swing system on daily bars.
Needs a first-N-minute opening range from a chosen anchor; not available. An independent replication on five indices found the gross edge disappears net of spread and slippage.
Needs time-of-day volatility bands from the session open and half-hour checks; not available. SPY-only evidence.
Needs time-of-day returns and clock-time entries; not available. For GLD the predictive half-hour is not necessarily the first.
Needs real traded volume to build VWAP; spot XAUUSD has only broker tick volume. Always-in-market flipping is extremely cost-sensitive. Unsuitable for GoldScalp's data.

Needs a 20-bar extreme at least 4 bars old; the nearest builder analogue (sweep of equal highs/lows or session levels) was already tested as VOL-F, R3 and R8, all rejected or not supported. No target in the source; daily-bar rules.
Needs RSI(2) at extremes (<= 5-10 / >= 90-95), a 200 SMA and a 5 SMA exit; the builder has RSI(14) confirmation only. No gold or intraday evidence; no stop in the original.
Needs Bollinger %b and a 200 SMA; not available. Academic evidence: Bollinger signals do not beat buy-and-hold after costs.
Needs Bollinger and Keltner bands and a momentum histogram; not available. The closest earlier analogue, R9 volatility-squeeze breakout, was rejected. No quantitative evidence.

Always-in-market crossover rules cannot be expressed (no crossover exit). The source's own evidence: standard parameters are not profitable even before costs; the best rules come from a 66,297-rule search (data-mining) with no costs. Not worth implementing.
Needs clock-time entries and exits (11:00 and 02:00 New York); not available. The source's net-of-spread returns fell to about 1.7% a year in 2013-18 and the effect is decaying.
